sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The injured claimant has challenged the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4055/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined compensation amount granted under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the MACT (Aux), Bhuj-Kutch by judgment dated 26.7.2010 in MACP no.694/07.

Mr. Modi for the claimant submitted that the Tribunal was required to follow the schedule under Section 163A of the Act to grant the compensation and any deviation from the same is not permissible and would be illegal.

2. Mr. Mazmudar submitted that there cannot be any quarrel to the provision of law and the mandatory provisions are required to be followed but at the same time, Mr. Mazmudar submitted that the amounts so granted by the Tribunal are just and reasonable in proportion to the physical injury suffered by the claimant.
3. The injured claimant was traveling in auto rickshaw bearing registration no. GJ-12 W-0091 on 29.9.2007.
It was stated by the claimant that respondent no.1 driver of the rickshaw was rash and negligent and was driving the vehicle in an excessive speed.

When they reached near Kotda telephone exchange at Nakhtrana, because of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4055/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined excessive speed, respondent no.1 lost control over the steering and suddenly the rickshaw turned turtle.
As a result of the accident, he suffered fractures and serious injuries on spinal cord and other vital parts of the body.

The claimant had stated that he was admitted for the treatment and the doctor had considered 70% injury while he states that 100%
functional disability was required to be considered since he lost his earning capacity.

Mr. Modi submitted that the Tribunal committed an error oblivious to the provisions of law and in case where the petition moved under Section 163A of the Act, the schedule attached has to be mandatorily followed to pay the compensation.
4. Having considered the submissions made by both the sides, perused the impugned order of the Tribunal, the Tribunal has granted the compensation as under:-
Rs.2,16,000/- Future loss of income Rs. 7,200/- Actual loss of income Rs. 7,000/-
Medical expenses NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4055/2010 JUDGMENT DATED:
17/01/2024 undefined Rs. 5,000/- Pain, shock and suffering Rs.2,35,200/- Total compensation

2 5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above computation has been made considering 50% permanent disability.
The age of the claimant at the time of the accident was 44.
The learned Tribunal has considered the schedule but had failed to grant the compensation as mandatorily provided in various age groups.

The Tribunal by taking into consideration the age had applied the multiplier as reflected in the schedule but had failed to observe that the schedule at the same time takes cognizance of the income limit and mandatorily provides for the compensation amount and following the same, the claimant has to be compensated.

6. In the present matter, the schedule considering the age of the victim between the age group of 40- 45 and for maximum annual income of Rs.40,000/- as has been pleaded in the present matter considers the compensation to be assessed as Rs.5,60,000/-.
The note of the schedule in a non-fatal case does not lay down any deduction under the head of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4055/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined personal expenses.

The doctor had considered 60%
permanent disability for the spinal cord and 10% for the left leg.

7. Having considered the vocation of the claimant as of being a driver and the Tribunal has observed the injury in the spinal cord and the leg, he would not be in a position to continue with his driving work.
This Court thus considers appropriate to assess the functional disability as 60% of the claimant.
8. The claimant has pleaded annual income of Rs.40,000/- and hence, as per the schedule considering the age of 44, total compensation amount comes to Rs.5,60,000/-.

Considering 60%
functional disability, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.3,36,000/-.
Further as per the schedule with the appended note under the head of pain, shock and suffering, an amount of Rs.5,000/- and an amount of Rs.15,000/- towards medical expenses are granted.

9. Considering the fact that the claimant had faced NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4055/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined the operations and the length of treatment, he would not have been in a position to recover for a period of 3 months and hence, amount of Rs.9,900/- is assessed as actual loss of income.

In the result, the computation is as under:-
Rs.3,36,000/- Future loss of income Rs. 9,900/- Actual loss of income Rs. 15,000/-
Medical expenses Rs. 5,000/- Pain, shock and suffering Rs.3,65,900/- Total compensation 10.

As the Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.2,35,200/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum, the claimant would be entitled to the enhanced amount of compensation of Rs.1,30,700/-
with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
The enhanced amount is directed to be deposited within eight weeks from the date of receipt of writ of this Court.
Let total amount be paid to the claimant on verification of the identity.
